experiment: Single-particle cryo-EM of BRD4-S/H4 K12acK16ac H3 K18ac nucleosome complex (GraFix cross-linked; 300 keV Titan Krios, K3 detector); focused 3D classification on BD1; local resolution compared between nucleosome and bromodomain
buffer: 10 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 20 mM KCl, 1 mM DTT
ligand_or_partner: Nucleosome (165 bp Widom 601, 10+145+10) containing H4 K12acK16ac and H3 K18ac; GraFix glutaraldehyde cross-linking (0-0.15% gradient)
construct_or_mutation: Human BRD4-S, residues 1-722, HIS tag removed by TEV protease; BD1 crystal structure (PDB 3UVX) built into the density
other_conditions: BRD4-S to nucleosome ratio 2.1:1; 80,704-particle class, 2.89 Å nominal resolution, about 4.5 Å local resolution for BD1; density seen for only one bromodomain (BD1); related structures: 3UVX, 3LZ0; deposited complexes 36IV and 36IU (basic patch 1 mutant) as listed by the authors
dynamics_type: domain-level flexibility/wobble of BD1 on the nucleosome; flexibility of BD2 and ET relative to nucleosome (ligand-bound complex heterogeneity)
author_claim: BD1 is tethered to the nucleosome through three contact points without a large interface, so the bromodomain is likely to wobble on the nucleosome, giving lower local resolution than the nucleosome, while BD2 and the ET domain are conformationally flexible and not visible.
anchor: difference in local resolution is often observed in nucleosome complexes
locator: Results, BRD4/nucleosome structure; Discussion; conditions: Methods, Cryo-EM sample preparation and data collection
caveat_note: Dynamics are inferred from lower local resolution (4.5 Å vs 2.9 Å), not measured, and no rate or population is determined. Reduced local resolution can also reflect partial occupancy or heterogeneity after classification, and the cross-linking step may restrict motion. Construct is full-length BRD4-S bound to a nucleosome, not the isolated BD1 of the entry. Residues R68, K72 and K76 are in full-length BRD4 numbering. Offset of 43 maps them to entry positions 25, 29 and 33, with matching residue types.

experiment: Native PAGE electrophoretic mobility shift (4.5% gel, EtBr stain) and Superdex 200 Increase size-exclusion chromatography of BRD4-S/nucleosome complexes, acetylated vs unmodified nucleosomes
buffer: 20 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 125 mM NaCl, 5 mM DTT, 5% glycerol, 0.01% NP-40, 0.01% CHAPS, 100 μg/ml BSA (gel shift); 10 mM HEPES pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, 0.1 mM PMSF (SEC)
ligand_or_partner: Nucleosome core particles, unmodified or H4 K12acK16ac (100 nM BRD4 variant with 100 nM nucleosome in gel shift; about 1 μM in SEC)
construct_or_mutation: HIS-tagged wild-type human BRD4-S (residues 1-722) and basic patch 1/BD1 mutants (m2 Y97F,N140A; m28 R68E,K72E,K76E; m11 and m12 basic patch 1 to Ala or Glu) compared
other_conditions: SEC peak elution volume 9.8 ml (BRD4-S WT/H4 K12acK16ac nucleosome) vs 9.6 ml (WT/unmodified nucleosome); BRD4-S m12 complex elutes earlier than WT; free BRD4 m12 elutes like WT; 30 min incubation
dynamics_type: ligand-coupled conformational change (compact vs less compact BRD4/nucleosome complex)
author_claim: BRD4-S adopts a more compact conformation on H4 K12acK16ac nucleosomes than on unmodified nucleosomes, and disrupting BD1 or basic patch contacts to the nucleosome makes the complex less compact and presumably more flexible.
anchor: complex migrates slightly faster when H4 K12acK16ac nucleosomes instead of
locator: Results, The conformation of the BRD4/nucleosome complex depends on histone acetylation; Figure 4d,g,h,i; Figure 5; conditions: Methods, Electrophoresis gel mobility shift assay and Size exclusion chromatography
caveat_note: Compactness is inferred indirectly from native-gel mobility and hydrodynamic radius, with no structural model of the alternate state and no exchange rate or population. Mobility also depends on charge, which the authors argue is not responsible, and the gel result for basic patch 5 does not track binding affinity. Cryo-EM densities for acetylated and unmodified complexes were not compared. The sample is full-length BRD4-S with a nucleosome, not isolated BD1. The restriction-enzyme assay showed no BRD4-dependent change in nucleosomal DNA-end accessibility, so the compactness difference does not involve DNA-end unwrapping.
